 By : Anshul October 22, 2026 | 10:38 IST Published On Oct 22, 2026 | 10:38 IST 
 Last Updated On Oct 22, 2026 | 10:38 IST

 AI Summary The 8th Pay Commission is consulting stakeholders now. While official fitment factors remain unannounced, final revisions depend entirely on upcoming government decisions.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source The 8th Pay Commission process is under way, but central government employees are still waiting for an official fitment factor and revised pay matrix.
 While the Commission gathers stakeholder inputs, employees can use different hypothetical fitment factors to understand how their current basic pay could translate into a revised amount.
 The 8th Central Pay Commission was constituted on November 3, 2025, and has 18 months to submit its recommendations.
 The Ministry of Finance has said the recommendations would normally be expected to take effect from January 1, 2026, following the usual 10-year cycle.
 This is not confirmation that revised salaries have been implemented from that date.
 How to calculate salary under the 8th Pay Commission 
 The simplest way to estimate revised basic pay is to multiply the current basic pay by an assumed fitment factor.
 Estimated revised basic pay = Current basic pay × Assumed fitment factor
 For example, if an employee's current basic pay is ₹30,000, a hypothetical fitment factor of 2.0 would give an estimated basic pay of ₹60,000.
 The factor used in this calculation is only an assumption. The Commission's recommendations and the government's final pay-fixation rules will determine the actual revision.
 8th Pay Commission salary calculator: Examples 
 The following calculations illustrate how different assumed factors would affect selected basic-pay amounts. 
 Current basic pay At 1.8 factor At 2.0 factor At 2.2 factor 
 ₹18,000 ₹32,400 ₹36,000 ₹39,600 
 ₹19,900 ₹35,820 ₹39,800 ₹43,780 
 ₹25,500 ₹45,900 ₹51,000 ₹56,100 
 ₹35,400 ₹63,720 ₹70,800 ₹77,880 
 ₹44,900 ₹80,820 ₹89,800 ₹98,780 
 ₹56,100 ₹1,00,980 ₹1,12,200 ₹1,23,420 
 These are mathematical illustrations, not official salary projections. They show basic pay only and do not account for allowances, deductions or the rules that will govern the revised pay structure.
 What can the 7th Pay Commission tell us? 
 The 7th Pay Commission recommended a fitment factor of 2.57, with minimum basic pay increasing from ₹7,000 to ₹18,000. The revised pay structure took effect from January 1, 2016.
 However, the 2.57 factor did not translate into a 157% increase in employees' overall salaries. The calculation incorporated the existing pay structure and Dearness Allowance (DA) neutralisation. The Commission's report put the actual increase after accounting for DA neutralisation at 14.29%.
 The previous revision is useful historical context, but it does not establish what factor the 8th Pay Commission will recommend.
 What is the latest status of the 8th Pay Commission? 
 The Commission is consulting stakeholders on pay, allowances, pensions and other service conditions. Its official website lists consultations in Mumbai on October 22–23, 2026. I t has 18 months from its constitution to submit its recommendations, placing the expected report timeline around May 2027.
 The fitment factor and revised pay matrix have not been officially announced. Any figures circulating online should be checked to establish whether they are employee-union demands, media estimates or government-approved decisions.
 8th Pay Commission salary and fitment factor: FAQs
 Will the 8th Pay Commission's salary revision apply from January 1, 2026?
 The government has stated that the recommendations would normally be expected to take effect from January 1, 2026, in line with the 10-year cycle. However, this is not the same as a formal implementation order confirming when revised salaries will be paid. Does the fitment factor determine an employee's take-home salary?
 No. It is used here to estimate basic pay. Actual gross and take-home salary will depend on the approved pay matrix, allowances, deductions and the government's final pay-fixation rules.
